_readme: Where a config path is anchored, defined once, in data.
Without this, each implementation invents platform behaviour: one expands '~', the other
reads %USERPROFILE%, a third falls back to os.homedir() — and the two tools disagree about
which file they are even looking at. That is precisely the drift the conformance suite is
meant to catch, so the fix belongs in the contract rather than in two codebases.
A registry entry names a `base` and a relative `path`. It never embeds '~' or '%VAR%'.
Resolution is: take the first env var in `from_env` that is set and non-empty; if none is,
use `fallback`. Segments join with the platform separator; the stored path always uses '/'.

project_root.description: The directory the scan was started from, or the nearest ancestor containing a project marker.
project_root._note: Ascends from the working directory to the first ancestor holding a marker, stopping at the home directory. If none is found, the working directory is used and no ancestor is searched.

app_config.description: Per-user application configuration. The one that genuinely differs per platform.

app_data.description: Per-user application state, distinct from configuration on Windows and Linux.

codex_home.description: Codex's home directory. Overridable, and the override is real: CODEX_HOME appears in the live config on the machine this was captured from.

rules._note: Registry entries store portable segments. A base whose env var is unset and whose fallback is null makes that location UNRESOLVABLE on that platform — reported as such, never guessed at.
